Text: ECMWF’s operational AI forecasting system can outperform physics-based models on several measures, including tropical cyclone tracks, while using roughly 1,000 times less energy to produce a forecast. #AI #Weather #ClimateTech

WHO says computer-aided detection software can automatically interpret chest X-rays for TB screening, helping expand case detection where specialist capacity is limited. #AI #GlobalHealth #Tuberculosis

European accessibility research highlights AI’s potential to adapt products and services to individual needs, supporting greater independence and participation for people with disabilities. #AI #Accessibility #Inclusion
Researchers used generative AI to design novel antibiotic candidates, with several synthesized compounds showing antibacterial activity against drug-resistant pathogens. #AI #Medicine #Antibiotics

UNESCO highlights AI tools that can support documentation, translation and revitalization of endangered and Indigenous languages when communities retain meaningful control over their data. #AI #Language #Culture
AI agents can help scientists classify complex material structures during experiments, accelerating research into better batteries, catalysts and other advanced materials. #AI #Science #Materials
AI image-analysis systems can identify signs of plant disease quickly, supporting earlier treatment and potentially reducing crop losses and unnecessary resource use. #AI #Agriculture #FoodSecurity
NASA’s ExoMiner++ uses AI to sift through huge space datasets and flagged thousands of potential exoplanet candidates for researchers to investigate. #AI #Space #Discovery

Researchers used deep reinforcement learning to adjust magnetic fields in real time and avoid disruptive instabilities in fusion plasma — a key challenge for future fusion energy. #AI #Fusion #CleanEnergy

UN experts highlight AI tools that can analyze satellite imagery and strengthen early-warning systems, helping responders assess damage and target assistance faster. #AI #DisasterResponse #EarlyWarning

NIST warns that indirect prompt injection can cause AI agents to follow malicious instructions embedded in data they process, potentially triggering unintended and harmful actions. #AI #Cybersecurity #Agents
The FBI warns that criminals are altering photos and other media to create fake proof-of-life material for virtual kidnapping scams and ransom demands. #AI #Deepfakes #Scams
The ILO warns that algorithmic management can intensify worker monitoring, shape task allocation and affect job quality when safeguards and worker protections are weak. #AI #Work #Surveillance
UNESCO’s work on AI bias warns that generative systems can reproduce gender stereotypes and enable technology-facilitated harms unless systems are actively tested and governed. #AI #Bias #Gender

The FTC found that surveillance-pricing systems can use information such as location, browsing behavior and shopping history to help tailor prices or promotions to individual consumers. #AI #Privacy #Pricing

The IEA projects global data-centre electricity consumption to roughly double by 2030, with accelerated servers driven mainly by AI accounting for a major share of the increase. #AI #Energy #DataCenters

The U.S. Copyright Office says unauthorized digital replicas pose serious threats to private citizens as realistic AI-generated images, video and audio become easier to create and distribute. #AI #Deepfakes #Identity

UN human-rights experts warn that AI-driven facial recognition can enable large-scale tracking and profiling, raising concerns about privacy, discrimination and freedom of movement. #AI #Surveillance #HumanRights

UNICEF warns that generative AI can produce convincing disinformation and synthetic media cheaply and at scale, including content personalized to influence individual users. #AI #Misinformation #Deepfakes
UNESCO cautions that AI language technologies can favor widely represented languages, while smaller and endangered languages may receive weaker digital support. #AI #Language #DigitalDivide
